findings.title: [P1] Configure the module to compile the queue source
findings.body: This POM uses Maven's default source root (`implementation/src/main/java`), but the only production source in the bundle is `implementation/M3CircularFifoQueue.java`. Consequently `mvn package` produces a JAR without `com/m3/collections/apache/M3CircularFifoQueue.class`, and the module verifier's class lookup fails. Move the source under the standard source tree or configure `sourceDirectory` explicitly.

findings.title: [P1] Add the Apache license resources required by the module
findings.body: The resource configuration expects `implementation/LICENSE.txt` and `implementation/NOTICE.txt`, but neither file is present in the change bundle. Maven therefore packages neither entry, causing `verify_module_public.py` to fail when it reads `META-INF/LICENSE.txt` and `META-INF/NOTICE.txt`; it also leaves the redistributed Apache-derived class without the notices the patch says are retained.

findings.title: [P1] Supply the source-binding specification used by the verifiers
findings.body: Both public verification scripts unconditionally load `qualification/source-bindings.json`, but that file is absent from the bundle. Every invocation terminates with `FileNotFoundError` before checking any source, provider JAR, or packaged module. Add the referenced specification, including the source and license records those scripts query.

findings.title: [P1] Invoke verification scripts that actually exist
findings.body: The workflow calls `verify.py` here and later calls `compare.py` and `verify_module.py`, while the bundle only provides `verify_public.py`, `compare_public.py`, and `verify_module_public.py`. Once the workflow is executed, each job fails at its first such invocation with a missing-file error. Rename the files or update every command consistently.

findings.title: [P2] Install the workflow under GitHub's workflow directory
findings.body: GitHub Actions only discovers workflow definitions under `.github/workflows`, but this definition is added as `qualification/workflow.yml`. As committed, pull requests and manual dispatches will never create these jobs, so none of the claimed contract, receiving-host, or module gates runs. Move it to the path already named in its own trigger configuration.

initialFixtureReview.overall_explanation: The queue implementation closely follows its donor, but the surrounding module and qualification bundle cannot function as committed: the module does not compile the source, required license resources and verifier input are absent, workflow commands reference nonexistent scripts, and GitHub will not discover the workflow at its current path. These are deterministic build and release-gate failures.

findings.title: [P1] Include the workflow file in the sparse checkout before verifying it
findings.body: Every job checks out only `m3/collections`, but `verify.py` iterates `source-bindings.json`, which includes `.github/workflows/m3-owned-apache-circular-fifo.yml`. That file will not exist in the sparse working tree, so verification raises `FileNotFoundError` before compilation or Maven runs. Expand each sparse checkout to include the workflow path (or remove that path from this verifier's required inputs).

exactRepositoryPathsReview.overall_explanation: The queue implementation appears consistent with its donor, but the newly added CI workflow cannot complete: all three jobs invoke a custody verifier that requires a file excluded by their sparse checkout.

correction.reviewFinding: v2-P1 workflow excluded by sparse checkout yet required by source binding
correction.runtimeRerun: not needed; owner and fixture bytes unchanged after executed exact-base replay

finalReview.overall_explanation: The multiline sparse-checkout configuration is valid for actions/checkout's default cone mode and now includes both the collection tree and the workflow path required by source verification in all three jobs. The bound workflow byte count increases by 132 bytes, matching the three identical 44-byte checkout expansions, and no actionable regression is evident in the supplied change bundle.

scope: original negative results retained; final paths/resources/bindings supplied; actual sparse omission reproduced and fixed; unchanged production Java runtime proofs reused
